habits.boundary_condition: Use the one-stop fallback when no nonstop itinerary exists or the nonstop fare exceeds the travel budget.
habits.condition: When searching for flights, prioritize nonstop options.
habits.default_action: Search for nonstop flights first; if they are unavailable or unaffordable, offer one-stop options and favor a manageable, shorter layover.
habits.exception_condition: Do not treat long or multiple layovers as equivalent fallbacks; surface layover duration and avoid extended airport time when alternatives exist.
habits.name: Prefer nonstop flights with a one-stop fallback
habits.preference_value: nonstop preferred; one stop acceptable when nonstop is unavailable or impractical
habits.rationale: Across three independent flight-planning conversations, the user consistently prefers nonstop service but accepts one stop when availability or price rules out nonstop travel, with attention to layover quality.

source_evidence.contribution: Establishes nonstop as the preferred default; the later acceptance of one stop after nonstop is unavailable supplies the fallback context.
source_evidence.exact_user_quote: I would like to go in business class and I would like to go nonstop if possible.

source_evidence.contribution: Explicitly states a reusable nonstop preference and permits connections when nonstop exceeds budget, while preferring limited airport time.
source_evidence.exact_user_quote: You know nonstop is always a preference of mine but I don't want to pay more than $1,600 roundtrip. So if you can't find it nonstop under $1,600 I'd say I'm willing to have a stopover or maybe two, but I don't want to spend to much time in other airports.

source_evidence.contribution: Directly confirms nonstop as the default and one layover as the acceptable connection limit.
source_evidence.exact_user_quote: I'd prefer non-stop but I'm okay with at most one layover.
